scenarios.title: Count tests for user authentication
scenarios.prompt: I need to understand how many tests we have for the user authentication feature. Our test suite has these files: auth.unit.test.js with testLogin, testLogout, testPasswordReset, testTokenRefresh, testSessionExpiry, testInvalidCredentials, testAccountLockout; auth.integration.test.js with testLoginAPI, testLogoutAPI, testOAuthFlow, test2FASetup, test2FAVerification; auth.e2e.test.js with testFullLoginFlow, testPasswordRecoveryFlow. How many tests do we have total and by type?

scenarios.title: Test distribution alignment check
scenarios.prompt: Our team has been following the testing pyramid model. We just ran our test suite and got: 45 unit tests, 25 integration tests, and 30 end-to-end tests. The total is 100 tests. Does this distribution follow best practices for the testing pyramid, or should we adjust our approach?

scenarios.title: Missing tests for shopping cart
scenarios.prompt: I'm worried we have gaps in our shopping cart testing. The cart should: add/remove items, update quantities, calculate totals with tax, apply discount codes, handle out-of-stock items, persist across sessions, and sync with inventory. We test adding items and calculating totals. What tests are we missing and how should we prioritize filling those gaps?

scenarios.title: Reviewing test quality for anti-patterns
Checking unit test completeness
scenarios.prompt: I just finished implementing a user authentication module with login, logout, and password reset features. I wrote unit tests for the login flow but I'm not sure if I've covered all the important edge cases. Can you review what I have and tell me what scenarios I might be missing? Here are my test cases: valid credentials, invalid username, invalid password, empty fields, and SQL injection attempt.

scenarios.title: E2E test scenario identification
scenarios.prompt: I'm building an e-commerce checkout flow and need to figure out what end-to-end tests to write. The flow includes: adding items to cart, entering shipping address, selecting shipping method, payment, and order confirmation. I already have happy path tests. What other E2E scenarios should I consider testing?

scenarios.title: Release readiness validation request
scenarios.prompt: We've completed development on our customer dashboard feature and want to validate that we're ready to ship. The feature includes data visualization, export functionality, and customizable widgets. We've done manual testing and have automated tests, but I want to make sure we haven't missed anything critical. What should we verify before giving the green light for deployment?

scenarios.title: Explain test coverage metrics
scenarios.prompt: I keep seeing coverage reports show 80% line coverage but we still have bugs in production. Can you explain what line coverage actually measures and what its limitations are? I want to understand why high coverage doesn't guarantee bug-free code.

scenarios.title: Fix failing unit test
scenarios.prompt: This unit test keeps failing and I can't figure out why. Here's the test: expect(calculateDiscount(100, 'PREMIUM')).toBe(20). The function should return 20 for a premium customer with 100 dollar purchase, but it returns 0. Here's the function: function calculateDiscount(amount, tier) { if (tier === 'premium') return amount * 0.2; return 0; }. What's wrong?

scenarios.title: Compare testing approaches
scenarios.prompt: Our team is debating whether to focus more on unit tests or integration tests for our microservices. We have limited time and resources. What are the trade-offs between these two testing levels? I need arguments for both sides so we can make an informed decision.

scenarios.title: Debug test environment issue
scenarios.prompt: My tests pass locally but fail in CI with a timeout error. The test suite has 50 tests and each one takes about 2 seconds. The CI timeout is set to 60 seconds. I'm using Jest with the default configuration. What could cause this discrepancy between local and CI environments?

scenarios.title: Payments module test coverage assessment
scenarios.prompt: I'm working on a payments processing module for our e-commerce platform. The module handles payment gateway integration, transaction processing, and payment confirmation callbacks. We have unit tests for the transaction logic, some integration tests for the gateway API calls, and a few end-to-end tests for the complete checkout flow. The requirements include supporting multiple payment methods (credit cards, PayPal, digital wallets), handling payment failures gracefully, and ensuring transaction idempotency. Can you review whether our current test approach adequately covers these requirements?

scenarios.title: Performance and security test coverage
scenarios.prompt: Our application requirements specify that the API must handle 5000 concurrent users with response times under 200ms, all endpoints must be protected against SQL injection and XSS attacks, and the system must maintain 99.9% uptime with automatic failover. We currently have unit tests for business logic and some integration tests for API endpoints. We're not sure if we need additional tests. Can you help us understand if our testing covers these requirements properly?

scenarios.title: Production release readiness check
scenarios.prompt: We're planning to release our React-based customer portal to production tomorrow. Our test results show: 85% unit test coverage, 70% integration test coverage, critical user flows (login, search, checkout) have 95% end-to-end test coverage, and all smoke tests pass. We follow the testing trophy model for frontend applications. Should we proceed with the release or do we need to address any gaps?

scenarios.title: Test coverage issues summary
scenarios.prompt: I just ran a coverage analysis on our authentication service and found several issues: some error handling paths have no tests, the password reset flow only has happy path tests, two API endpoints are missing integration tests entirely, test naming could be more descriptive, and the OAuth callback handler has no tests. Can you summarize these findings for my team?

scenarios.title: Finding untested edge cases
scenarios.prompt: I just finished implementing a user authentication module with login, logout, password reset, and session timeout features. My team wrote tests for the happy paths but I'm worried about edge cases. We have unit tests for valid credentials, integration tests for database connections, and one E2E test for the login flow. What test scenarios should we add to feel confident about edge cases and error handling?
